# The `question` frame — the contract `ai.js` is built against

This is the wire contract for a reply that stops to ask the person something.
The UI half (PRD 5.2) is implemented in `ai.js` beside this file; the API half
(PRD 5.1) has not been written yet. **This document is the specification 5.1
must satisfy** — it was settled from the person's side first, deliberately,
because the API half was built first once and had to be parked: a question
pause with no UI does not degrade, it freezes the chat.

It lives here rather than under `docs/` because `docs/` is the public SDK site
published to developers.workpeg.com; this is an internal contract between two
halves of one feature, and it belongs next to the file that consumes it.

Since PRD 7.7 the vocabulary below is also DECLARED on the server, in
`chats/frames.py`: `QUESTION_KEYS`, the three states and the frame's per-state
shape live there (re-exported under their old names from `chats/prompts.py`),
and `chats/tests/test_frame_contract.py` derives what is actually emitted and
replayed and compares it against that declaration. §1's key list and its
`state` comment are read out of THIS FILE too, by
`tests/ui/test_frame_drift.py`, and compared to the same registry — so a key
or a state added on one side and not the other fails rather than drifts.
This document remains the reasoning; the registry is the machine-checked
half of it.

Everything below is binding on the server unless it says otherwise. Where the
parked branch `wip/5.1-questions` (42f8cac) already does the right thing, it is
called out — those parts are contract now, not preference, so they do not get
re-litigated.

## What adversarial verification of the UI moved in this contract

Read these first if you have read an earlier draft. Each one was reproduced
against the real runtime, and each one is now covered by a test with a
mutation twin in `tests/ai/ai_surface.test.mjs`.

| Was | Is | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the step is "every field of the frame except `type`" | the fold is an **allowlist of eight keys**; `kind` and every `_` key are the client's | §2 |
| `options` shape left to the wire sketch | an **invariant**, and the client treats a non-array as no options | §1.3.6, §6 |
| the card leans on the sentence being in `content` | the open card **echoes `text` itself** when the bubble has not | §1.3.5, §7 |
| `finishStream` replaces the trail wholesale | it **merges**: an `answered` question never regresses to `pending` | §2.1 |
| `commitStream` marks the reply finished | a server-confirmed `generating: true` **survives**, so a dropped socket is not a missed question | §4.1, §5 |
| *"This question wasn't answered."* for anything settled | **only** for a step the server marked `expired` | §4.1, §5 |
| three sync sites | **four** — `attachStreamTail` shares `paintStream`'s gate | §4.3 |
| answerability is state + lock + live | plus **the card actually rendered** — nothing may claim a pause the screen could not show | §4.1 |

---

## 0. The one-paragraph version

A reply pauses by emitting a `question` frame and folding an identical
`question` step into its durable `activity` trail. The client renders a card
from the **step**; the frame's only job is to get the step into the client's
copy of the trail while the reply is live. The person answers by POSTing to
`answers/<message>/`. The answer is written into the step, so it is still on
screen after the turn ends and after any later reload. A client that has never
heard of a question ignores the frame and shows the question as prose, because
the question sentence is also spoken into the reply's own `content`.

---

## 1. The `question` frame

Emitted through `_event_frame`, i.e. `data: __WP_EVENT__<json>__END_OF_CHUNK__`.

```jsonc
{
  "type":        "question",     // required, literal
  "id":          "call_abc123",  // required, stable for the question's whole life
  "message":     "<uuid>",       // required — see §1.1, this one is not optional
  "state":       "pending",      // required: exactly one of pending|answered|expired
  "text":        "Which account…?",  // required, non-empty, <= 500 chars
  "options":     [ /* Option */ ],   // required key; [] for an open question
  "allow_other": true,           // required bool; a HINT to the surface (§3)
  "asked_at":    "2026-08-14T10:00:00Z",  // required, ISO-8601 UTC
  "answer":      { /* Answer */ }         // present IFF state == "answered"
}
```

```jsonc
Option = {
  "id":    "0",          // required string; server-stamped by index
  "rank":  1,            // required int, 1-based, == array order (informational)
  "label": "Operating",  // required non-empty string, <= 120 chars
  "why":   "used last"   // optional, <= 200 chars. Absent — never null — when empty
}

Answer = {
  "option_id": "1" | null,     // required key; null when they only typed
  "label":     "Payroll"|null, // required key; the SERVER's copy of the chosen label
  "text":      "",             // required string, possibly ""; their own words, <= 2000
  "at":        "2026-08-14T10:01:00Z"  // required, ISO-8601
}
```

### 1.1 `message` is required, and this is the load-bearing addition

A reply that is still streaming has the client-side id `"streaming"` until
`finishStream` reconciles it against `messages/latest/` — and for a paused turn
that has not happened and will not for the fifteen minutes the tail stays open.
So on the one path where a question actually arrives live, the client has no
message id to POST to. Without `message` on the frame, the card either posts to
`/answers/streaming/` or cannot be offered at all.

`ai.js` prefers `step.message` and falls back to `msg.id`; when neither is
usable it renders a read-only card reading *"Reload the page to answer this
question."* — honest, and a reload genuinely repairs it, because the resumed
tail is built against the reply's real id. That is a degradation path, not a
licence to omit the field.

### 1.2 Changes from the parked branch, and why

* **`message` added.** §1.1.
* **`asked_at` added.** A question in history with no time cannot be placed in
  the conversation. `Answer.at` already existed; the ask side had nothing.
* **`Answer.label` split from `Answer.text`.** The parked branch writes the
  chosen option's label *into* `text`, so the record cannot tell "chose
  Payroll" from "typed Payroll", and cannot carry "chose Payroll **and** added
  a note". The card renders both halves (`You chose Payroll` plus the note);
  the trail shows both. `label` is copied server-side from the stored option
  and is never taken from the request body.
* **`options` and `allow_other` are required-present.** The parked branch
  always emits them but never says so. A client that has to write
  `(ev.options || [])` is a client that will one day have to guess whether an
  absent key means "open question" or "server too old".
* **No `version` field.** Forward compatibility is carried by the unknown-state
  rule in §5 instead — one less thing to keep in step.
* **No `expires_at`.** It was considered and rejected: the reconciler's window
  is a CLI flag and can drift from anything stamped into a frame, and a
  question past a stale `expires_at` that the server still accepts must still
  work. The client does no arithmetic on time at all (§4.2).

### 1.3 Invariants binding on the server

1. **Frame and step are information-equivalent by construction.** Keep them as
   one dict with a different discriminator key (`_question_payload` /
   `_question_step` on the parked branch already are). Test it as set-equality
   of keys, not field by field. The reason is real: `finishStream` replaces
   `aiMsg.activity` wholesale with the server's at end of stream, so anything
   that lives on a frame but not in a step is destroyed the moment the turn
   ends — and for a question, the options and the answer *are* the interface.
2. **The ask call emits no `tool_call` frame and folds no `tool` step. Ever.**
   Every ai.js on the CDN turns any step with `kind: "tool", state: "pending"`
   into *Allow once / Always allow / Decline* and lets it POST an approval verb
   at the pause. The parked branch's gate is correct and is now contract.
3. **Question frames fold by `id`, last write wins**, mirroring the server's
   own `_fold_step`. This is load-bearing: a resumed turn seeds its buffer with
   the existing one, so a client reloading mid-resume receives the `pending`
   frame *and then* the `answered` frame for the same id, and must end up with
   one card.
4. **The step must keep the field name `text`, at the top level.** An ai.js
   with no `question` renderer falls through to `content.innerHTML =
   renderMarkdown(s.text || s.kind || "")`. Rename the field and the whole CDN
   fleet prints the literal word `question` in the Activity drawer.
   Corollary: **never promote `label`, `why` or `answer.text` to a step key
   called `text`** — the fallback reads exactly `s.text` and every other key is
   inert on an old client. Adding a `text`-keyed sub-object later would be a
   new markdown sink on a fleet nobody can redeploy.
5. **The question sentence stays in the reply's `content`.** That is the whole
   old-client degradation story: a reply that reads as a question rather than
   one that stops mid-thought, and something for `text_from_buffer` and
   `ai_reconcile` to salvage. It is **no longer load-bearing for the card**:
   an open card now echoes `text` itself whenever the bubble above is not
   already carrying it (§7). That change was forced. The old design leaned on
   two server preconditions and neither is binding — `content` must be
   *flushed to the row* before the frame goes out (§8.1, never traced), and on
   a reload the sentence must be re-replayed as **tokens**, because
   `resumeReply` builds the reply with `content: ""` and `loadConversation`
   drops the server's stored copy. When either fails the person was shown a
   *Recommended* badge and three account names with no question anywhere on
   the screen: an unlabelled multiple choice where one click commits and
   nothing undoes it. Keep the sentence in `content` for the old-client story;
   the card no longer depends on you doing so.
6. **`options` is a JSON array or the key is absent — never a string, an
   object or a number.** This is stated as an invariant rather than left to
   §1's shape sketch because it was reachable: the fold writes what arrived,
   three paths reach it (the frame, the 202/200 echo, the 409 body), and a
   server echoing a stored `jsonb` step reaches it too. The client no longer
   depends on it — anything that is not an `Array` reads as no options at all
   (§6) — but a server that sends one has sent a question nobody can pick
   from, which is a bug on that side and should be caught there.
7. **No presentational field, ever.** The frame carries no `icon`, `glyph`,
   `variant`, `color`, `style`, `class` or URL of any kind. `icon()` in ai.js
   builds `"ti ti-" + name` with no scrub, unlike the SDK's own `_ICON_RE`, so
   any such field would be a class-injection sink in Workpeg's own chrome.
   **Stating the absence of those fields is the security control.** A future
   per-option icon must be a server-mapped enum, never a name the model writes.

---

## 2. The durable step

```jsonc
{ "kind": "question",
  "id": …, "message": …, "state": …, "text": …,
  "options": …, "allow_other": …, "asked_at": …, "answer": … }
```

Folded on `(kind, id)` — the kind belongs in the key because a question and the
tool call that asked it share a call id.

**The fold is an allowlist, and that list is exactly the eight keys above.**
It used to read "every field of the frame except `type`, identically", and the
client implemented it literally. That was a hole. `kind` is what every renderer
on this surface dispatches on, and three separate wire paths reach the fold —
the SSE frame, the 202/200 echo and the 409 body — so any of them could rewrite
it. Observed, against the real runtime:

* a `question` frame carrying `kind: "thinking"` re-kinds the step: the card
  disappears entirely and the model's `text` goes to the Activity drawer's
  markdown sink, which renders a live off-platform anchor;
* a `question` frame carrying `kind: "tool"` with `state: "pending"` becomes
  the *Allow once / Always allow / Decline* row — §1.3.2 is a server rule and
  the client was enforcing nothing;
* a 409 body writing `_note` lands verbatim in the one line of the card that
  speaks in **Workpeg's own voice**, bypassing every cap and the bidi strip;
* a 202 echo that re-kinds the step erases the person's receipt on the
  *success* path.

So: `kind` is set by the client, never taken from the wire; `type` is dropped;
every `_`-prefixed key is client-private and unwritable. Adding a field to this
contract means adding it to that list on purpose. If 5.1 needs a new key, say
so here and it gets added — a server cannot take one.

**Normalisation must happen at settle time, not at read time.** The parked
branch rewrites `pending → expired` only in the tail's settled-replay branch,
which is not the path a reload of a settled reply takes: that goes
`GET .../messages/` → the serializer publishes `activity` raw → `renderAiMessage`
reads `msg.activity`. Meanwhile the reconciler clears `stream_buffer` and
`pending_turn` but never touches `activity`. So a swept reply's history says
`{"kind":"question","state":"pending"}` on a failed message, permanently.

Add one helper — `expire_questions(activity)` — that rewrites every `pending`
question step to `expired`, and call it on **every** transition out of
`Message.LIVE_STATES`:

* the reconciler's 24-hour sweep,
* `approvals.decline`, reached from both `AnswerView` and `ApprovalView`,
* the tail's own idle-timeout settle,
* `resume_generation`'s failure path.

Keep the read-time rewrite as a **backstop** for rows written before this ships.
It stops being the mechanism and becomes the safety net.

The client does not depend on any of this (§4.1) — but the durable record must
not lie, because it is what the trail, the audit and every future consumer read.

### 2.1 A lagging trail may not un-answer a question

`finishStream` replaces `aiMsg.activity` wholesale with the server's at end of
turn, and that is right for every other kind: the server's record is the
record. For a question it threw away strictly better information. The answer
POST and the `messages/latest/` read race, so a trail still reading `pending`
overwrote the `answered` step the client had just folded **from the endpoint's
own authoritative 202 echo**, and the receipt reverted to the settled fallback
sentence. That is the regression 5.2 exists to prevent, arriving through the
back door.

The client now merges rather than replaces (`mergeServerActivity`): server
order, server fields, except that

* a question this client knows is `answered` never regresses to anything else,
* the client-private flags a refusal set (`_locked`, `_note`) survive, because
  the server cannot know them,
* a question the server's copy has never heard of is appended, not dropped.

Nothing regresses the other way: a server that says `answered` when the client
does not know it is simply telling the client something new, and is believed.

This is a **backstop, not a licence**. A trail that contradicts an answer the
endpoint accepted is still a bug on the server side, and §2's settle-time
rewrite is still the mechanism.

---

## 3. The answer endpoint

```text
POST /v1/businesses/<business_uuid>/chats/<chat_id>/answers/<message_id>/
```

Its own path, not a verb on `approvals/`. The two claims filter on different
pause kinds, and that is what makes an answer *structurally* unable to resume a
turn waiting on an approval. The parked branch got this right.

Auth: the same shape `approvals/` accepts. `ai.js` sends
`credentials: "include"`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and **no CSRF
header** — it has none to send, and cannot be fixed from ai.js if this diverges.

### Request

```jsonc
{ "question_id": "call_abc123",  // required
  "option_id":   "1",            // optional
  "text":        "…" }           // optional
```

At least one of `option_id` / `text` must be present and non-empty. **Both
together are legal**: the option is the choice, the text is a note. The parked
branch returns on `option_id` before ever reading `text`, silently discarding
what the person typed — the worst available outcome for a ranked-option UI with
a free-text field beside it.

`option_id` must name an option this question actually offered, checked against
the stored question **before** the claim, so a malformed body cannot burn a
pause that is still perfectly answerable.

Free text is accepted **whatever `allow_other` says**. `allow_other` governs the
affordance; the endpoint governs authority. A model must not be able to close a
person into a set of choices it wrote itself. The parked branch's reasoning here
is right and is contract.

### Responses

| Status | Body | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `202` | `{"state":"generating","message":"<uuid>","question":{…answered…}}` | accepted, a worker is resuming |
| `200` | `{"state":"done","question":{…answered…}}` | accepted, but the resume could not start |
| `400` | `{"code":"…","detail":"…"}` | malformed body |
| `409` | `{"code":"…","detail":"…","question":{…authoritative…}}` | the claim failed |
| `404` | — | message not found, or not this staff member's |

`code` is stable and machine-readable and is never localised. `detail` is the
human sentence and may be translated — `ai.js` shows it verbatim on a `400`.

* `400 question_missing` — no `question_id`
* `400 option_unknown` — an `option_id` that was never offered
* `400 empty_answer` — neither an option nor any text
* `409 already_answered` — the stored step is `answered` (another tab)
* `409 expired` — the reply has settled with the question unanswered
* `409 not_waiting` — anything else, including an approval-kind pause

**This is the change from the parked branch**, which collapses every claim
failure into one `400` with a prose string. On one status code a client cannot
tell "another tab answered — here is what they said" from "the reconciler swept
this", and two of the six states the UI must handle become unreachable. `400`
and `409` mean opposite things to the client: re-enable and let them retry
versus settle read-only and stop offering.

A `410` for the expired case is acceptable if it is cheaper server-side; the
client treats every non-401 4xx that is not a 400 identically.

The `409` body carries the authoritative question, read back from `activity`
after the failed claim, so the tab that lost renders the truth with no second
request. The reply-level prose deliberately does not say *which kind* of pause
it was not waiting on — keep that; the `code` carries the machine distinction,
and the sentence must not tell somebody which button they should have pressed.

**Retry is always safe and needs no idempotency key.** The claim is a single
conditional `UPDATE`, so a retry after a POST whose response was lost loses the
race and is refused rather than answering twice. Stated here because otherwise
somebody will add one.

That property is the reason the client can be honest about a second POST
rather than merely unlikely to send one — and it was needed. The client's
double-submit guard used to live only in the closure of the card's DOM, and
`syncQuestions` discards that closure whenever the card is rebuilt (which
happens *with the card still open* — a question re-emitted with a different
option count, or a second question arriving beside it). The rebuilt card came
up armed and posted the same `question_id` twice. The guard now lives on the
step as well, so a card rebuilt underneath an in-flight POST comes up
disabled. **The server must still refuse the second one**; the client is a
courtesy, not the mechanism.

### What `ai.js` does with each

| Status | Client |
| --- | --- |
| 202 / 200 | fold the echoed `question` into the step, render the receipt, rejoin the reply |
| 400 | re-enable the controls, keep the typed text, show `detail` beside the field |
| 401 | nothing — `request` already refreshed the token and retried |
| other 4xx | **do not re-enable**; settle read-only from the echoed question, or say it was answered elsewhere |
| network / 5xx | re-enable, keep the text, offer *Try again* |

The answer shown is always the **server's echo**, never the local input: the
endpoint strips control characters, removes the frame delimiter and truncates
at 2000, and showing text the server did not store is a receipt for the wrong
thing.

---

## 4. What the client does that the server can rely on

### 4.1 Answerability is decided twice, and the client half is independent

```text
answerable(msg, step)  ⟺  step.state === "pending"
                          && step is not locked by a refusal we already saw
                          && the card for this step actually rendered
                          && replyIsLive(msg)

replyIsLive(msg)       ⟺  msg is the reply this client is streaming right now
                          || msg.generating === true
```

The third clause is not decoration. Answerability drives the **composer**, and
the composer reads the step, not the card — so a question the UI could not
render left the send button genuinely `disabled`, the placeholder reading
*"Answer above to carry on"*, and a blocked Enter searching for a card that
was never built. That is the 5.1 freeze restored, and worse, because the
composer now actively points at nothing. **Nothing may claim a pending pause
the screen could not show.** A card that fails to build renders the read-only
*"Reload the page to answer this question."* card in its place and releases
the composer.

`Message.generating` is a derived property (`state in LIVE_STATES`) already on
the wire for every message. A settled reply is `false` and is **not answerable
whatever its trail says** — which closes §2's history hole client-side even if
the server regresses. A streaming reply is recognised by identity against the
open stream, because a message this client invented has no `generating` key at
all; a message read back from the server must say `true` *positively*.

The direction is deliberate. Under-offering an answer box costs a reload;
over-offering one costs somebody an answer the endpoint refuses.

**`generating` on `messages/latest/` is load-bearing at the end of a stream.**
When the fifteen-minute tail limit drops the socket on a still-pending
question, `finishStream` fetches the reply and the server says
`generating: true` — the pause is still open, the endpoint will still accept
an answer for hours. `commitStream` used to stamp `generating = false` over
exactly that, so the card in that tab settled and read *"This question wasn't
answered."* about a question that still could be — character-for-character
identical to a genuinely expired one — while the composer unlocked and invited
a turn that orphans the pause. It no longer does: a reply the server has
**positively confirmed** is still running keeps `generating: true`, the card
stays answerable, and the composer stays honest. Answering from there takes
§4.4's re-tail path, which needs nothing from the server.

So `messages/latest/` must report `generating` truthfully for a paused turn.
It is the only signal that tells "your connection dropped" apart from "you
missed it", and the client has no other.

Where the client genuinely cannot tell — a reconcile that failed, a swept
reply whose trail was never rewritten, a state added by a later server — the
card says *"Reload the page to answer this question."* and **never** claims
nobody answered. Only a step the server itself marked `expired` earns that
sentence. This is the client-side reason §2's settle-time rewrite matters: it
is what puts the truthful sentence on the screen.

### 4.2 The client never computes expiry

`state` is server-authoritative. The fifteen-minute tail limit reclaims a
**socket**, not a pause — an answer at T+20min may legitimately succeed — so
`ai.js` runs no clock of its own and greys nothing out on one. `asked_at` is
displayed at most; it is never a gate.

### 4.3 Where the card is synced from

Four sites, all reading `msg.activity` and never stream state:
`renderAiMessage` (history and full re-renders), `paintStream` (the live
arrival), `attachStreamTail` (a remount of a live thread) and `commitStream`'s
in-place update (the turn ending). Neither of the middle two is optional:
`paintStream` builds the reply node once and then rewrites only the bubble, so
a card built only by `renderAiMessage` appears on a reload and never on the
live turn — which is most of the original freeze restored.

`attachStreamTail` runs when a shell re-render wipes the host under a live
thread, and it decides between the reply node and a thinking indicator. It
made that decision on `aiMsg.content` alone while `paintStream` had been
widened to `content || questionSteps(aiMsg).length` against exactly this
threat, so a pause whose bubble was still empty came back as a spinner with
the composer still locked. **Both gates are `content || a question step`, and
they have to move together** — hardening one of two sync sites against a
threat and not the other is the defect, whatever the server usually does.

### 4.4 Rejoining after an answer

If this client's tail is still open, nothing happens: the resumed worker
appends to the same stream buffer and the frames simply start arriving again.
Otherwise the client does exactly what a reload does — drop the reply from the
thread and re-tail it. The server needs to do nothing special for either.

### 4.5 The composer

The composer stays **locked** while a question is pending on the visible thread
(it already is — `S.sending` is true for the whole paused turn), but it now
says so: a real `disabled` on the send button, a placeholder reading *"Answer
above to carry on"*, and a blocked Enter that scrolls to the card and pulses it
instead of doing nothing.

Routing composer text to the answer endpoint was rejected: the composer is the
conversation channel and an answer is a tool result bound to a specific
`question_id`, so "actually stop, forget it" would be recorded as the answer to
"which account?".

**Server-side follow-up, not in this contract:** the client cannot stop somebody
starting a new turn that orphans a pause (a background stream, a second tab).
5.1 should decide what a new user message in a chat whose last reply is
`awaiting_input` does to the pending question.

---

## 5. Every state, and what produces it

| State | Server condition | How it reaches the UI | What renders |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| live pending | `awaiting_input`, step `pending` | `question` frame on the open stream | the card, answerable |
| reload while pending | same | the tail replays `stream_buffer` from 0, frame included | the identical card |
| remount while pending | same | no new traffic; `attachStreamTail` rebuilds from state | the identical card (§4.3) |
| history, answered | settled, step `answered` + `answer` | `msg.activity` | read-only receipt: *You chose Payroll* |
| history, expired | settled `FAILED`, step `expired` | `msg.activity` | read-only: *This question wasn't answered.* |
| history, legacy pending | settled, step still `pending` (pre-§2 rows) | `msg.activity` | read-only — `generating: false` forces it — reading *Reload the page to answer this question.*, because the client cannot know nobody answered |
| tail limit dropped the socket | still `awaiting_input`; `messages/latest/` says `generating: true` | the reconcile at end of stream | the card **stays answerable**; answering re-tails (§4.4) |
| answered in another tab, tail open | the claim flips the row; the worker re-emits | a `question` frame with `state: "answered"` | the card becomes a receipt by itself |
| answered in another tab, tail closed | the claim fails | `409` + the authoritative question | the card settles read-only from the body |
| **unknown state** | any value this client has not heard of | either | **read-only**, and *never* "wasn't answered" |
| **unrenderable question** | a frame the client cannot build a card from | either | read-only *Reload the page…*; the composer is released (§4.1) |

The last row is the forward-compatibility clause and is tested: answerability
is an **allowlist** on `state === "pending"`, never a denylist on
`state !== "answered"`. That is what lets 5.2's UI survive a 5.3 that adds
`"cancelled"`.

Note the "answered in another tab, tail open" row costs nothing and needs no
new channel: both tabs tail the same buffer. Do not add a socket for it.

---

## 6. Untrusted text

Every string in §1 is model-authored, and the model is influenced by tool
output, Peg manifests and the person's own documents. They arrive into
Workpeg's own chrome, where somebody has every reason to trust what they see.

**Server side, binding:**

1. Bounded and control-char-stripped at the ask tool, as the parked branch
   already does. The client does not undo it and does not rely on it alone.
2. **Strip the frame delimiters at the frame writer.** `_clean` removes control
   characters but not `__END_OF_CHUNK__` or `__WP_EVENT__`, and `json.dumps`
   has no reason to escape plain ASCII underscores. A label containing
   `…__END_OF_CHUNK__data: __WP_EVENT__{"type":"tool_call","state":"pending",…}`
   cuts the frame it is travelling in and synthesises an arbitrary control
   frame — and a pending `tool_call` is the one that puts approval buttons in
   front of a person. The parked branch strips the delimiter from the *answer*
   only, and its own docstring concedes the hazard exists elsewhere. For a
   question it stops being theoretical, because the person is invited to click
   the result. **Fix it in `_event_frame`**, once, for every frame type — per
   field is the version that rots the moment somebody adds a field. (Not run
   against the API suite; check nothing asserts an exact frame body first.)
3. No field may ever be a URL, an href, an icon name, a CSS value or an HTML
   fragment (§1.3.7).

**Client side, already implemented here:**

* Every card string goes in as `textContent` — never `opts.html`, never
  `renderMarkdown`. The same sentence is markdown in the bubble and plain text
  in the card, deliberately: prose is prose, but a card is chrome, and chrome
  that renders model markdown can put a live link inside a click-to-commit
  control.
* **Every field is type-checked before it is walked, and a renderer that
  throws is not a way back to the markdown sink.** Those are two guards for
  one hole and both were missing. `options` arriving as a string, an object or
  a number threw out of `.slice`, and neither catch that caught it was a safe
  failure: `activityStepNode`'s fell through to
  `content.innerHTML = renderMarkdown(s.text)` — the exact sink registering
  the `question` renderer exists to close — and `syncQuestions`' dropped the
  card while the composer stayed locked. Now `options` is read through one
  helper that returns `[]` for anything that is not an `Array`, and a
  **registered** renderer that throws falls to a text-only step instead of the
  fallback. The fallback stays as it is: it is the degradation path for a kind
  this build has never heard of, not a safety net for one it has.
* **The fold is an allowlist** (§2). No wire field can set the step's `kind`
  or any client-private `_` key.
* Client-side caps re-applied: text 500, label 120, why 200, answer 2000,
  six options.
* **Bidi overrides (U+202A–U+202E) are stripped** and every model-authored
  element carries `unicode-bidi: isolate` and `dir="auto"`. The server's
  control-character class stops at U+007F, and an RLO in a label can make it
  display as its neighbour — a real spoof in a list where one click commits.
  The bidi **isolates** (U+2066–U+2069) are deliberately kept: they are the
  modern, non-spoofing construct a genuine mixed Arabic/Latin label needs, and
  the CSS isolation contains their effect to their own element anyway. Strip
  what spoofs; keep what a real label uses.
* The only heading on the card is client-owned copy, so the model's text never
  occupies a heading slot. The card is always inside the AI message — never
  full-bleed, centred, modal, or over the composer — so it cannot imitate
  Workpeg's own UI. No danger or primary styling is reachable from data.
* Incognito hides the composer's approval pill, not the card. Asking is not
  acting, so a question is legitimate in incognito, and hiding it there would
  make incognito an unanswerable freeze.

### 6.1 "An old ai.js already ignores a question" — corrected

True of the **frame**: `handleEvent` is a flat chain with no default branch, so
an unknown `type` is parsed, matched against nothing and dropped.

**False of the step.** The step reaches old clients twice — `finishStream`
replaces `activity` wholesale with the server's, and history renders `activity`
directly — and with no `question` entry in `STEP_RENDERERS` the fallback runs
`renderMarkdown(s.text)` into `innerHTML`. So **an old ai.js renders the
question's text as Markdown in the Activity drawer**, which can produce a live
off-platform link. `renderMarkdown` escapes first and gates every href through
`safeHref`, so it is not a script hole — and the marginal exposure is nil,
because that same string is already markdown-rendered in the bubble. But it is
displayed, not ignored, and it is why §1.3.4 is a hard rule rather than a
preference. A new ai.js registers a `question` step renderer; old ones keep
doing the other thing and nothing in this contract can change that.

### 6.2 The other direction — a new `ai.js` inside an OLD app

Nothing here binds 5.1, but it is the half of §1.1 that is easy to forget, and
both traps were live in the first cut of this UI.

* **A new icon name is a blank square in the fleet.** `_runtime_base_icons()`
  in `build.py` scrapes icon names out of the *bundled* runtime JS at build
  time and `_subset_icons_css` writes a per-app, content-hashed `icons.css`
  containing only those rules. An app built before 5.2 therefore has no rule
  for a name only the new `ai.js` mentions — and this is invisible from in
  here, because a fresh build always contains it. The pending glyph was
  `help-circle`, which appears in no previous runtime file; it is now `help`,
  which is in `scaffold.js` and `workpeg-runtime.js` and so is present
  whatever an app's `ai.js` age. Only fully-static-icon apps are affected —
  dynamic-icon apps link the CDN's full sheet. There is a test.
* **Anything appended unconditionally costs every reply.** The `wpai-questions`
  container is added to *every* AI message so the sync always has somewhere to
  fill, and `.chat-message__content` is a 6px-gap flex column in which an empty
  flex item still spends its gap. Against a server that has never emitted a
  question, every reply in every chat grew 6px taller. `:empty{display:none}`
  is the fix and the file's own existing idiom. The rule to carry forward: a
  new node on a shared path must be inert when the feature is absent, and
  "renders nothing" is not the same as "occupies nothing".

---

## 7. Design decisions the UI made, that the contract now depends on

* **Order is the rank.** `rank` is stamped from the array index server-side, so
  the two are one fact. The card sorts by array position and ignores `rank`
  entirely, which deletes the class of bug where the two disagree. `rank` stays
  in the frame as **informational** for the answer receipt and non-UI
  consumers; **the UI must not sort by it.**
* **One click answers**, rather than radios plus a Send button. A confirm step
  taxes every correct answer to save a rare misclick, and the misclick is
  bounded: the resumed turn still runs under the same approval rules, so a
  wrong answer cannot silently perform a dangerous action.
* **The open card asks the question when the bubble has not.** It compares
  `step.text` with the reply's `content` (both normalised the way the card
  shows them) and echoes only when the sentence is not already a few pixels
  above. It errs towards showing: the same words twice is cosmetic, and an
  unlabelled irreversible multiple choice is not. §1.3.5 has the two server
  preconditions this replaced, and why neither was safe to depend on.
* **The first option is marked "Recommended", and only the first.** Numbering
  every row reads as steps, or as a priority the person is expected to respect,
  and invents precision between #2 and #3 that the model did not have.
* **The free-text field is always reachable.** With `allow_other: true` it is a
  row of the same list; with `allow_other: false` it is demoted behind one
  quiet affordance, never removed — because the endpoint accepts free text
  regardless, and hiding it would hand the model a power the server denies it.
* **Arrows move focus and never commit**, and the options are `<button>`s in a
  `role="group"` — not a `radiogroup` or `listbox`, both of which select on
  arrow, and this activation is irreversible.
* **A settled card lists no alternatives.** Six inert rows in a scrolled-back
  thread is the strongest possible "looks answerable but isn't". The full list
  lives in the Activity trail.
* **The answer is not written into `content`.** It lives on the durable step.
  Cost, said plainly: an ai.js older than 5.2 shows the question and the
  continuation with no record of what the person said. The alternative —
  appending their words to the assistant's bubble — is a provenance lie and a
  second markdown sink for text the endpoint does not strip markdown from. A
  judgement call, not a derivation.

---

## 8. Open questions for whoever implements 5.1

1. **Does `Message.content` actually carry the question sentence at the moment
   of pausing?** It was not traced from this side. It is no longer load-bearing
   for the card — §1.3.5 — but the old-client degradation story still rests on
   it entirely, so it is still worth an answer.
   **Related, and binding:** does `messages/latest/` report `generating: true`
   for a turn sitting in `awaiting_input`? §4.1 now depends on it to tell a
   dropped socket from a missed question.
2. **Does stripping the delimiters in `_event_frame` perturb any existing test
   that asserts an exact frame body?** One line, every frame type.
3. **The ToolMessage id fallback.** `_ask_the_person` takes `call_id or name`
   and the resume replies with `question["id"] or ASK_QUESTION`. If a provider
   ever returns an empty call id, the transcript gets a `ToolMessage` whose
   `tool_call_id` is the tool *name* and matches no call. No test covers it.
4. **Endpoint scoping.** `AnswerView` filters chat + owner but not
   `business_uuid` — identical to `ApprovalView`, so not a new hole, but
   whether `IsBusinessStaff` binds the URL's business to the staff row was not
   chased.
5. **Whether cron actually runs the reconciler at the 24-hour default in
   production.** Only the default was read.
6. **What a new user message does to a pending question** (§4.5).
